- **Johnny Newton (DT)** — Dan Quinn said in April he believes Newton is “about to absolutely take off,” and Newton says his Week 17 finish against Dallas — three sacks of Dak Prescott — has given him a real confidence boost entering Year 3. He also moved into the first team late last season, which points to a more established role and more snap volume in an aggressive front. [5]

- **K’Lavon Chaisson (EDGE)** — A Commanders roundup framed Chaisson as a potentially underrated addition, with a clear path to production if Odafe Oweh draws the bulk of attention opposite him. The fantasy angle is limited to IDP leagues, but the role signal is that Chaisson could be a meaningful pass-rush contributor if Washington’s front generates pressure as hoped. [2]

- **Quan Martin (S)** — Martin’s safety job is still unsettled; Washington wants training camp to sort out whether he can be trusted in the secondary when the pads come on and the defense is communicating at full speed. It’s not a final verdict, but it does make his starting-caliber role a legitimate camp battle to watch. [1]
